subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering the Periodic Table & isotopes, air pollutants & combustion, substance properties & bonding, carboxylic acids & relative molecular mass, ethanol & fermentation, electrolysis of HCl, rates of reaction, and metals & compounds.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question:
The diagram shows part of the Periodic Table containing H, K, Ca, N, O, F, Al, Cl, Br, I, Ar, Pt.
State the symbol of the element that is a fuel which is a gas at room temperature.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: State the symbol of the element that is used to kill bacteria in water.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: State the symbol of the element that forms a stable ion of type X3+.

parts.label: a(iv)
parts.question: State the symbol of the element that is a grey-black non-metallic solid at room temperature.

parts.label: a(v)
parts.question: State the symbol of the element that forms an ion which, on addition of aqueous sodium hydroxide, gives a white precipitate which is soluble in excess aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Identify one correct statement about isotopes. Tick one box.
options: They are molecules with the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
They are atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
They are molecules with the same number of protons but different numbers of electrons.
They are atoms with the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: An isotope of sulfur is shown: ³³S₁₆. Deduce the number of protons and neutrons in this isotope.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Complete the electronic structure of a sulfur atom. (Draw the electron shells for sulfur: 2,8,6)

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question:
The table shows mass of air pollutants (oxides of nitrogen, sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, ozone, particulates) in 1000 cm³ samples over four months (Aug-Nov).
Name the pollutant that shows a decrease in concentration between August and November. (Aug: 29.5, Nov: 12.8)

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Calculate the mass of oxides of nitrogen in 250 cm³ of the sample of air taken in August. (August NOx = 106.0 ng in 1000 cm³)

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Carbon monoxide is produced by the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels. State the meaning of the term incomplete combustion.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Give one adverse effect of carbon monoxide on health.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Carbon monoxide is also produced when methane reacts with steam in the presence of a catalyst. Explain why a catalyst is used in this reaction.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Methane is an air pollutant. State one source of methane in the air.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question:
Complete the chemical equation for the reaction of carbon monoxide with oxygen.
____ CO + O₂ → ____ CO₂

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Complete the energy level diagram for the reaction of carbon monoxide with oxygen by writing reactants and products on the diagram. (Reactants at higher energy, products at lower energy)

parts.label: d(iii)
parts.question: Explain, using information on the energy level diagram, how you know that this reaction is exothermic.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.question: Describe a test for carbon dioxide.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.question: Identify which one of these pH values represents the pH of a solution of carbon dioxide in water. Draw a circle around the correct answer.

parts.label: a
parts.question:
Table shows properties of four substances A, B, C, D:
A: does not conduct solid or molten, low mp, insoluble
B: conducts solid and molten, high mp, insoluble
C: does not conduct solid or molten, very high mp, soluble
D: does not conduct solid, conducts molten, high mp, soluble
State which substance, A, B, C or D, is sulfur. Explain your answer.

parts.label: b
parts.question: State which substance, A, B, C or D, is sodium chloride. Explain your answer.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question:
The structure of crotonic acid is shown (a 4-carbon chain with a C=C double bond and a -COOH group).
On the structure, draw a circle around the functional group which shows that this is an unsaturated compound.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Deduce the formula of crotonic acid to show the number of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms. (Structure: CH₃-CH=CH-COOH)

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question:
Complete the table to calculate the relative molecular mass of crotonic acid.
carbon: 4 × 12 = 48
hydrogen: __ × 1 = __
oxygen: __ × 16 = __
relative molecular mass = ____

parts.label: b
parts.question:
Complete the word equation for the reaction of nitric acid with calcium oxide.
nitric acid + calcium oxide → ____ + ____

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Calcium oxide is manufactured from limestone by thermal decomposition. Give the name of the main chemical compound in limestone.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: State the meaning of the term thermal decomposition.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Calcium oxide reacts with water to produce slaked lime. State one use of slaked lime.

parts.label: a
parts.question: The formula of ethanol is C₂H₆O. Draw the structure of ethanol to show all of the atoms and all of the bonds.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Ethanol is a liquid at room temperature. Describe the motion and separation of the particles in ethanol.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Name the two products formed when ethanol undergoes complete combustion.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Ethanol can be manufactured by the fermentation of glucose. One condition is using enzymes in yeast. State two other conditions for fermentation.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Name the method used to separate the ethanol from the reaction mixture after fermentation is complete.

parts.label: e
parts.question:
Alcohols can also be manufactured from alkenes. Complete the word equation for the manufacture of ethanol by this method.
____ + ____ → ethanol

parts.label: a
parts.question: Describe the electrolysis of concentrated hydrochloric acid. Include a labelled diagram of the apparatus used for the electrolysis and collection of gases, and the names of the products formed at the positive and negative electrode.

parts.label: b
parts.question:
Complete the chemical equation for the reaction of hydrochloric acid with sodium carbonate.
Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → ____ NaCl + ____ + CO₂

parts.label: c
parts.question:
Carbon dioxide reacts with carbon to produce carbon monoxide: CO₂ + C → 2CO.
Explain how this equation shows that carbon dioxide has been reduced.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: A student investigated the rate of reaction of excess calcium carbonate with dilute HCl by two methods. Method 1: measure volume of CO₂ at intervals. Method 2: measure loss in mass at intervals. Suggest one advantage of Method 1 compared with Method 2.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Explain why there is a decrease in mass of the reaction mixture in Method 2.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: The graph shows volume of CO₂ against time for large pieces of CaCO₃ (curve starts steep, then levels off at 50 cm³). Describe how the rate of this reaction changes with time.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Deduce the time taken to collect 36 cm³ of carbon dioxide from the graph.

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: The experiment is repeated using smaller pieces of calcium carbonate. All other conditions stay the same. Draw a line on the grid to show how the volume of carbon dioxide changes with time when smaller pieces are used. (Steeper initial slope, same final volume)

parts.label: b(iv)
parts.question:
Describe what effect the following changes have on the rate of this reaction. All other conditions stay the same.
● The temperature is increased.
● The concentration of the hydrochloric acid is decreased.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Sodium is a metal in Group I of the Periodic Table. Identify two correct statements about sodium. Tick two boxes.
options: It is a relatively soft metal.
It has a high melting point.
It has a lower density than most metals.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question:
Some changes of state of sodium are shown: solid sodium → R → liquid sodium → S → sodium gas.
Give the names of the changes of state represented by R and S.

parts.label: b
parts.question:
Table compares reactions of four metals with dilute and concentrated HCl:
beryllium: bubbles form rapidly / bubbles form very rapidly
copper: no bubbles seen / no bubbles seen
iron: bubbles form very slowly / bubbles form slowly
nickel: no bubbles seen / bubbles form slowly
Put the four metals in order of their reactivity. Put the least reactive metal first.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Crystals of magnesium chloride, MgCl₂·6H₂O, can be prepared by adding excess magnesium powder to dilute hydrochloric acid. Describe how to prepare a sample of pure dry magnesium chloride crystals after the reaction is complete. Include how to remove excess magnesium, crystallise the magnesium chloride, and dry the crystals.

parts.label: d
parts.question:
Complete this description of the test for sulfur dioxide using words from the list: blue, chloride, colourless, green, manganate(VII), sulfate(VI).
The test for sulfur dioxide uses acidified aqueous potassium ____. The colour change is from purple to ____.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.question:
Green nickel(II) sulfate crystals turn yellow when heated: NiSO₄·7H₂O → NiSO₄ + 7H₂O.
Suggest how you would change yellow nickel(II) sulfate to green nickel(II) sulfate.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.question: Identify which word best describes green nickel(II) sulfate with the formula NiSO₄·7H₂O. Draw a circle around the correct answer.
